pageCache.text:
Welcome to New Regent's College
At New Regent’s College, our mission “Learning to Succeed” sits at the heart of everything we do. We work with young people who may have faced significant challenges in their education and who are at risk of disengagement or underachievement. Our role is to help them rediscover confidence in learning and to equip them with the skills,attitudes, and qualifications they need to move forward successfully.
We believe every young person can succeed when they are supported with respect, responsibility, and resilience. These values guide our relationships, our expectations, and our approach to learning. We treat every learner with dignity and understanding, encourage them to take responsibility for their choices and progress, and help them build the resilience needed to overcome barriers and thrive.
For many students, their time with us is a short but important chapter. Most learners attend New Regent’s for a limited period before returning to mainstream education, transitioning to a new school, or moving on to post-16 pathways.
During their time with us, we focus on removing barriers to learning, whether these relate to behaviour, emotional wellbeing, attendance or gaps in learning, so that students are ready for their next step.
There is a strong emphasis on literacy and numeracy, particularly for our younger learners, as we recognise these as essential foundations for future success. Although we are a mixed-age provision, primary-aged pupils are educated separately from secondary students, ensuring age-appropriate learning and support. All students benefit from small class sizes and high levels of individualised support, allowing strong relationships to develop between staff and learners. For our older students in Years 10 and 11, education may take place on site or through a carefully selected range of specialist vocational providers. We work closely with each student with the ambition that all Key Stage 4 learners achieve five GCSEs or equivalent qualifications, including English and Mathematics, wherever this is appropriate to their starting points and needs.
Some students are referred to New Regent’s by their school so that we can provide a curriculum or specialist support that may not be available in their home setting. Every learner receives independent advice and guidance to support informed decisions about education, training or employment beyond Year 11.
We are proud of our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We strive to ensure equality of opportunity for every member of our college community, regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or belief, social class, ethnicity or language. Our community is enriched by its diversity, and we work actively to ensure that everyone feels safe, valued, and respected.
In September 2019, we moved into our purpose-built campus, providing first-class facilities that support learning, wellbeing and personal development. Our environment reflects our belief that young people deserve high-quality spaces in which to learn, grow, and succeed.
We hope this website provides a helpful introduction for parents, carers, students and the wider community. At New Regent’s College, we are committed to supporting every young person to continue Learning to Succeed, now and in the future.

Key Stage 1&2
Our Curriculum Mission
Our curriculum at New Regent’s College Primary has the following aims:
We strongly value the principals of the Nurture Group Network and aim to teach utilising meaningful and purposeful links, which offers pupils breadth of opportunity for deeper learning. This ensures that pupils acquire and develop a range of skills which are underpinned by knowledge and practical experiences.
There is ongoing development of a ‘mastery’ curriculum where pupils have multiple opportunities to return to content, over time, in order to gain fluency in the core curriculum. For example, during ‘Green Time” and Friday Enrichment learning activities facilitate pupils in revisiting ideas and concepts in a variety of situations in order to slowly develop an understanding over time. Our teaching staff members work collaboratively to ensure that skills are progressively taught throughout the school, ensuring that expectations of pupils are high and appropriately challenging. The content of our curriculum is customised to meet the needs of our pupils.
There is a strong emphasis on providing pupils with opportunities to engage in learning within the community and through carefully planned enrichment activities.
This is to add value to learning and maximise participation in community activities. This prepares them for the challenge of being an active citizen. Frequent visits and trips are organised regularly throughout the year to complement classroom teaching.
The teaching in phonics and reading is supported by a range of interventions and teachers have adapted their own schemes using Read, Write Inc., Letters and Sounds and Jolly Phonics. In order to further support the development of reading and writing skills and, develop a love of reading, each class starts the afternoon with a daily reading session to promote reading for pleasure.
Key Stage 1: Mars Class
Lower Key Stage 2: Pluto
Upper Key Stage 2: Neptune Class

Launch of MyTutor Programme
We have launched a personalised on-line interactive Tutor programme at New Regent’s College. We felt our pupils needed a focused intervention to catch up on the English and Maths lessons they missed due to the Covid-19 lockdown.
Called MyTutor, they match pupils with a top tutor to reinforce classwork, boost confidence and raise grades. They currently work with over 400 schools. Latest Impact Report from MyTutor has shown that pupils can make twice the grade progress of their peers, helping pupils to fulfil their potential as a result.
It was a successful launch where pupils engaged well with the lessons and responded positively to the tailored 1 to 1 support. Because pupils have the same tutor, they develop a strong relationship and rapport – this builds confidence and really helps them improve.

Key Stage 3
Our Key Stage 3 curriculum follows a thematic approach, with topics explored across all curriculum areas. This allows learners to apply their learning in a range of creative, practical, and academic ways, helping them to make meaningful connections between subjects and the world around them.
Creativity and hands-on learning are central to our approach. Lessons are designed to build confidence and motivation and re-engage pupils who may have found learning challenging in the past. Through varied teaching approaches and strong relationships, we support students to develop curiosity, resilience, and a positive attitude to learning.
Our theme of "Strong Foundations" is designed to equip students with the essential knowledge, skills, and values necessary for their academic and personal growth. By focusing on building robust foundations across all subject areas, we aim to foster a deep understanding and a love of learning that will serve as a springboard for future success. English: This unit develops Strong Foundations in reading, writing and discussion through contemporary and heritage short texts from the Diverse Shorts anthology. Pupils explore themes of power, justice, control and freedom through narrative voice and perspective, developing empathy, critical literacy, and understanding of real-world social issues.
Maths: This unit builds Strong Foundations in number and estimation, developing skills in rounding, significant figures, and truncation. Pupils explore rounding errors and inequalities, extending prior work with integers to decimals and building confidence in accuracy and problem-solving.
STEM: This theme builds Strong Foundations in scientific thinking by sparking curiosity about the “hidden worlds” of science. Students explore microbiology, unseen forces and early scientific discoveries, developing their research skills and confidence in communicating scientific ideas.
Science: This unit builds Strong Foundations in biology and scientific skills through the study of the human digestive system. Pupils explore tissues, organs, enzymes, and beneficial bacteria,while developing skills in data interpretation, risk evaluation, and improving investigations.
PE: This unit builds Strong Foundations in physical skills and fitness. Pupils take part in individual and paired activities to develop agility, balance, coordination, endurance, strength,flexibility, power, and reaction time, with lessons designed to be active, engaging, and inclusive.
Art: This unit builds Strong Foundations in creativity and visual expression through the theme of Architecture. Pupils design and create a 30cm × 30cm card model of a real or fictional location, exploring foreground, mid-ground, and background features while developing planning, composition, and artistic skills.
RE: This unit builds Strong Foundations in understanding religion and history through the study of Christianity in the UK. Pupils explore the British Empire and historical attitudes to religion, developing knowledge, critical thinking, and the ability to consider different perspectives.
PSHE: This unit builds Strong Foundations in health, wellbeing and resilience. Pupils explore physical and mental health through balanced diets, exercise and healthy lifestyles, while examining eating disorders and the influence of social media to help them recognise risks and develop strategies for resilience.

Key Stage 4
The New Regent’s College Key Stage 4 Programme offers alternative education for students in year 10 and 11. TheKey Stage 4 Programme offers full-time education placements for students who are referred by Hackney Education and Hackney Schools.
Specialisms in the team include wellbeing and progression mentoring, special educational needs, careers advice, attendance support, quality and curriculum monitoring and school and family liaison. Our team offer interventions and support with a number of issues that are affecting young people today, such as returning to school post Lockdown, personal safety, healthy relationships, managing emotions, relationships building and preparation for education, work and training.
We have a variety of programmes available to meet the needs of our young people. These programmes range from full time GCSE to vocational courses including a multi-skills construction course, music production, health and social care and hair and beauty. We have a brand new Key Stage 4 facility on the Nile Street site, which will be suitable for those students who are able to access a GCSE programme with some aspects of vocational studies.
In addition, we have small providers who offer a pastoral, nurturing environment, as well as larger college style providers who can offer a more mainstream experience. We are also able to offer bespoke programmes to suit students with specific needs. All of our providers are adept at offering support for students that find themselves outside of mainstream education and need help with both behaviour and/or learning needs. Our providers are listed here in the Hackney Education Alternative Pathways Directory.
We work in close partnership with professional agencies, Speech, and Language Therapists, Educational Psychologists, CAMHS, Hackney’s Wellbeing and Mental Health in Schools (WAMHS) project, Social Care, Virtual School, Young Hackney, Attendance and Educational Welfare Officers and the police to ensure students receive the wrap around support they require.
Currently our subject offer is:
GCSE English GCSE Maths GCSE Biology GCSE Citizenship
GCSE Religious Education GCSE Food NCFE Level 1 / 2 Art & Craft Cambridge National Level 1 / 2 Sport Science BTEC Level 2 Digital IT Functional Skills Level 1 or 2 in ICT Functional Skills Level 1 or 2 in English Entry Level Certificate in Maths Core Physical Education
Our school day is from 9.45am-3.30pm and begins with breakfast club at 9:00am and then tutorial; first lesson begins at 10:15am. Lunch is at 1:20pm for forty minutes. Students wear full school uniform and personal possessions, including mobile phones, are collected on arrival to be securely locked away for the duration of the day. Students remain onsite throughout the whole school day. If students remain with us on site they are based in either a year 10 or year 11 classroom for core subjects and then use our state-of- the-art facilities such as the Sports Hall and the ICT Suite for other subjects. Lunch is provided in the dining room.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Restorative Learning School (RLS) - New Regent's College
pageCache.text:
The Restorative Learning School (RLS)
The Restorative Learning School (RLS) offers a full-time educational placement for pupils who are on fixed-term suspension. We can receive LAC and vulnerable pupils on the first day of suspension and other pupils on the sixth day of suspension. Please contact the RLS team for further details.
At The Restorative Learning School, we provide a positive, high quality, calm and work-focused learning environment. This enables pupils to refocus on their education. Pupils have the opportunity to catch up on work they may have missed and to re-engage with their learning. It is an opportunity for schools to provide work for the pupil, which they need to complete in order to facilitate a smooth return to school. We will provide age and level-appropriate work in Maths, English, Science and other subjects.
Our approach is to promote independent learning and encourage reflection. A quiet working environment provides the space for pupils to reflect on why they have been suspended and what they need to do to put things right. It is this reflective process that has the most impact.
We adopt restorative approaches to resolve conflict and repair relationships. Pupils have the opportunity to talk about the reason for suspension and what they could have done differently at the initial interview. At the hand-off interview they have the opportunity to share their reflections and how their time with us will influence future behaviour at school.
Parents and carers play an integral part in ensuring their children behave well at RLS. We contact both the referring school and parents for any breaches in our Code of Conduct.

Our role is to help them rediscover confidence in learning and to equip them with the skills, attitudes, and qualifications they need to move forward successfully.
